title: Creating Python datetime and time Objects
learningObjectives: Explain constructing time and combined datetime values and its role in Python applications.
Choose appropriate datetime classes and methods for constructing time and combined datetime values.
Predict the output of representative PY17.3 operations.
Identify invalid values, formatting ambiguity or timezone risks related to constructing time and combined datetime values.
Apply constructing time and combined datetime values in a small, deterministic Python program.

understand.concept: A time object stores clock fields, while a datetime object combines calendar and clock fields. Constructors accept optional seconds, microseconds and timezone information. Use `datetime.combine()` when a date and a time are stored separately, and distinguish naive values from timezone-aware values.
understand.whyItMatters: Many applications schedule events, store appointment times or compare timestamps. Choosing clear date-time values avoids mixing calendar dates with clock-only values.
understand.analogy: Date-time values are like entries on a calendar plus the hands on a clock; a duration measures the distance between two entries.
understand.analogyLimit: Real calendars include leap years, time zones and daylight-saving transitions that a simple wall calendar analogy does not fully model.
understand.summary: Creating Python datetime and time Objects teaches reliable representation and manipulation of Python date-time values.

explain.narrative:
## Build a time value
Use `datetime.time(hour, minute, second, microsecond)`. The fields are validated and can be read from the resulting object.

## Build a datetime value
Use `datetime.datetime(year, month, day, hour, minute, second)`. Omitted time fields default to zero. A datetime can be naive or timezone-aware.

## Combine separate values
`datetime.combine(date_value, time_value)` creates a datetime from a date and a time. This is useful when a calendar day and a daily schedule are maintained separately.

## Naive versus aware
A naive datetime has no timezone information. An aware datetime has a usable UTC offset. Do not compare naive and aware datetimes as if they represented the same kind of value.

examples.title: Create a time with seconds
examples.code:
from datetime import time
alarm = time(6, 45, 30)
print(alarm.hour)
print(alarm.minute)
print(alarm.second)
examples.explanation: Clock components are available as named attributes.

examples.title: Create a datetime with a specific time
examples.code:
from datetime import datetime
appointment = datetime(2026, 7, 8, 14, 5)
print(appointment)
examples.explanation: The datetime constructor combines date and time fields.

examples.title: Combine a date and a time
examples.code:
from datetime import date, time, datetime
day = date(2026, 12, 1)
clock = time(10, 15)
slot = datetime.combine(day, clock)
print(slot)
examples.explanation: combine creates a datetime from separate date and time objects.

examples.title: Inspect timezone awareness
examples.code:
from datetime import datetime, timezone
naive = datetime(2026, 1, 1, 12)
aware = datetime(2026, 1, 1, 12, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
print(naive.tzinfo)
print(aware.utcoffset())
examples.explanation: A UTC-aware datetime has a zero UTC offset.

examples.title: Validate a time field
examples.explanation: Hours must be in the valid 0 through 23 range.

questions.prompt: Which class represents a clock time?
questions.explanation: time stores hour, minute, second and microsecond.

questions.prompt: Which method combines a date and a time?
questions.explanation: combine creates a datetime from date and time objects.

questions.prompt: What does a naive datetime lack?
questions.explanation: A naive datetime has no timezone offset information.
timezone.utc represents UTC with a zero offset.

questions.prompt: What happens if hour=25 is passed to time()?
questions.explanation: Valid hour values range from 0 through 23.
